answer: Epoch replay consistency rule grants full weight only when an identity’s current actions match its hash-chained record from prior epochs. A new identity must replay K epochs of workload before voting or earning, and a spiral of divergent actions throttles it until a consistency proof is accepted. A random beacon anchors each epoch’s record hash so histories cannot be backfilled cheaply. The gale of verification work is paid per identity: N sybils cost N×K replay compute and storage, so each extra identity adds linear cost.
